Came over, not so much because of the Reddit drama recently, but more because the site came up a lot over there and I wanted a public space with less of the hivemind and more opinion and discussion.

I am pretty open with my online footprint so here is a bit about me.

I am a 21 year old Physics and Astro-Physics student at the University of Exeter in Southern England. I have just completed my 3rd year of a 4 year combined masters course and with current predictions I am set to come away with a First Class Honours degree (about a 4.2 GPA/Latin Honours). I have a strong interest in both the sciences, and also in history, particularly medieval and classical Europe. If I was living in the states, I would likely be called either an Independent or a Libertarian, but really I have a wide selection of different political ideals and I vote on policy, not party. Around election time you will find me emailing my local candidates on the issues they DONT talk about. This led to my voting Green in my area in the last (and my first ever) general election. On the topic of faith, I am somewhere between an atheistic- and agnostic-theist, that is I am not really asking the question of if there is a God, and I side more with their not being one, but I am open to the concept and feel that if there was anything, it is unlikely to be a being more than an originating force. I have a long term, long distance girlfriend in California and I intend to live in that area of the world after my degree, with plans for a career in observational cosmology.

I think that covers just about everything. Just ask if you want to know anything else. I will answer what I am comfortable with answering.
Welcome albions-angel, we hope you have a great time here! Why are you study physics?

Its a bit of a funny story. My family used to holiday in Florida a lot when I was growing up. At about 7 years old, I wanted to be a palaeontologist because I liked dinosaurs, or a soldier because I liked "shooting bad guys". Then one day in Florida, I get woken up by my dad at 4 am local time, put in the car and driven to a cold, dark jetty in the middle of the swamp. I had no idea what was going on. We stood there for about 15 minutes, some more people turned up, all just looking across the swamp. And then there was this bright light. The most beautiful white light I have ever seen. Lit up the tree line across the swamp. And rising above it, this bright star, climbing slowly, gracefully towards the sky. And then the water began to shake, little droplets rising from its surface, and my chest began to resonate with a sound I couldnt hear, and then I was hit with a wall of noise so throaty and deep. It was awe inspiring.

What I witnessed was the first successful launch of the Delta 3 rocket. It was followed by spending the day at Kennedy Space Centre, walking the length of the Saturn V, meeting an astronaut, seeing the construction of a satellite, visiting the launch pads. It was wonderful. But I was still a bit, well, meh, about the whole thing. And as we were leaving, a VHS catches my eye and I buy it and bring it home and watch it. Its October Sky: The dramatic retelling of the story of the "Rocket Boys", a handful of boys from a mining town in West Virginia who beat the odds and escape a life of coal mining to become scientists at NASA. And while I am from a well off family, and my sleepy village wasnt really like WV, it spoke to me. From then on the dream was "rocket scientist".

I was good at maths and science; very good at them. I excelled academically. But always the goal was to lean physics and astro-physics. And the more physics I did, the more cemented the dream became. Now I am living it, and loving it. I can code, write papers, analyse data, peer review, design structures, engineer devices; I could walk away now and enter more or less whatever field I wanted, and be fairly successful. But nothing feels like completing the last part of an analysis on a protostellar cluster and breaking new ground. That sense of scientific discovery is amazing. And as a student, I have access to the latest information. I am right there, at the face, on the cliff edge, holding a torch for humanity to see by, and beside me, not in front of me, but side by side, are other torch bearers: Students, Professors, Scientists, Academics, Theorists, all there, all treating me as an equal, and together we keep pushing forward the darkness.

Thats why I study physics. Because I get to be the first to see the new things, and decide what they are trying to tell us. I get to be an explorer, like Drake and Cook, but my jungle is the Universe, all of existence. And I love it.
Who knew one experience can give you such a powerful dream. Well I give good luck to you for find more about this universe!
Thank you! Good luck to you too!
